To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number and density of Na+ channels increase with age during mouse brain development.

Na+ channels are widely expressed in fetal brain cells at an early stage (day 13 of fetal life) and that the subsequent increase in receptor capacity is due to a combination of an increase in the number of labeled cells and in the receptor density of the labeled cells.

Na+ channels are present in a large population of mouse brain cells as early as day 13 fetal life, and that this early expression of Na+ channels is followed by a progressive increase in both receptor number and density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of the Na+ channel during brain development.
the expression and cellular distribution of the Na+ channels during mouse brain maturation and provides a quantitative basis for future studies in the developing nervous system.
the early appearance of Na+ channels and their distribution at the cellular level in the mouse brain during development.
